findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the small ice machine had an accumulation of soil residues on the front of interior baffle and behind it. PIC was notified and a staff member started the process of cleaning it. Staff and PIC determined that a more professional cleaning would be needed. Ice machine was removed from service and PIC will buy bagged ice from an approved source. Facility will use bagged ice until ice machine can be thoroughly serviced. Ensure equipment food-contact surfaces are kept clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed that the right 2-door freezer in the back area had a significant accumulation of ice at the bottom. PIC was notified, had already noticed the ice accumulation, and was actively planning to move the items inside to a different freezer so that the 2-door freezer could be cleaned. Ensure nonfood-contact surfaces are cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil residues.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee used their bare hand to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated when the action was observed. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed several rubber spatulas that were cracking and chipping. The PIC voluntarily discarded the spatulas during the inspection. They were educated that damaged equipment must be discarded if they pose a risk of contamination. Ensure that food is always protected from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the sanitizer dispenser (sink and surface sanitizer; lactic acid) was not dispensing at the correct concentration. The district manager contacted EcoLab to schedule repairs during the inspection. The PIC will be making the sanitizer buckets manually until it is serviced. The inspector will follow-up on 9/22/2025 to check that the sanitizer dispenser is dispensing at the correct concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed there is an accumulation of dirt, outside residue, and other debris on the floor underneath the triple freezer by the back exit door. Physical facilities must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the floor is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
THIS IS A THIRD REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that not all employees have food handler certificates. All employees who do not have the CFPM (certified food protection manager) certificate must complete basic food handler training. Ensure that all employees have food handler certificates by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Person-in-charge was unable to answer basic food-safety questions regarding cold-holding in the facility. Critical temperature ranges were not being properly monitored as indicated by temperature logs indicating temperatures above the 41 degree threshold. Operator has been advised that as person-in-charge, they are responsible for the following:

The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (A) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations not conducted in private home/room with sleeping quarters;  (B) restricted access ; (C) visitors comply with Code; (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;  (F) approved source/unadulterated;  (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ; (I) monitoring temperatures; (J) consumer advisory conveyed; (K) proper sanitizing;  (L) buffets are controlled;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of responsibility to report information about health; (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. Pf  

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

** Due to the severity of the violations observed and a general lack of food safety knowledge regarding cold holding temperatures and managerial responsibilities, a follow-up is issued for 30-days to ensure ongoing compliance with ALL priority/priority foundation items.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Inspector observed cartons of milk in the milk cooler adjacent to the dry storage area to be holding between 45 and 55 degrees F for an unknown period of time. Logs indicate temperature abuse with no corrective actions on 11/3 (42F), 11/6 (45F), 11/9 (42) and 11/13 (45). A hanging thermometer was placed in the cooler but was damaged and not functioning properly. Logged temperatures have been taken using built-in thermometers and not using internal hanging thermometers as required. Operator was unaware of the requirement that TCS foods must be maintained below 41 degrees and has been relying on Prairie Farms for verifying proper functioning of this equipment. Milk stored within the cooler has been discarded. Canned pears (opened) recently placed in the cooler (within the past hour) have been moved to an alternative location for the time being. Juice held within the cooler does not require refrigeration for safety and has not been discarded. A follow-up has been issued for 3-days to ensure proper cold holding. Inspector will return on Thursday 11/16/2023. Ensure that ALL cold held foods are stored at or below 41 degrees F at ALL times. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Compliance with variance/specialized process/HACCP
findings.comment:
Facility operates under a HACCP plan but is unable to provide a copy of the plan itself. Person-in-charge on arrival is unaware of the requirements of the HACCP plan. Records have been photocopies with staff initials, dates, and temperatures indicating that false temperature records are being kept. A follow-up is being issued for 3-days to ensure that the person-in-charge is aware of the HACCP plan, the requirements of the HACCP plan, proper recordkeeping, and IMMEDIATELY ceases keeping false records. 

8-103.12: If AUTHORITY grants VARIANCE, PERMIT HOLDER shall: (A) comply with HACCP PLAN (P) (B) Maintain and provide records (PF).

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
The hanging thermometer stored in the milk cooler is observed to be broken and thus displaying incorrect temperatures. Staff has been checking external thermometer when checking temperatures for logs. Thermometers must be available and accurate at ALL times to ensure proper cold holding. A follow-up has been issued for 3-days to ensure that all coolers have proper internal hanging thermometers and that such thermometers are functioning properly. Inspector will return on 11/16/2023. 

4-203.12: (A) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be accurate to +/- 1.5C. (B) accurate to +/- 3 Fahrenheit.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
During the previous inspection performed on 05/09/2023, the facility was cited for cleaning in hard-to-reach areas such as under the sinks and behind/under equipment. This is a repeat violation and persists during the inspection today. Ensure that these areas are cleaned often enough the preclude the accumulation of residue and debris. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a kitchen employee using a personal cell phone at the counter where food preparation occurs. Employee was wearing gloves while using the personal phone. The gloves were removed, but employee failed to wash hands prior to working with food. The act of removing soiled gloves, especially gloves soiled by exceptionally contaminated items such as cell phones, results in potential contamination of the hands during removal. Ensure that hands are washed between glove changes and immediately before returning to food preparation. Inspector discussed the violation with person-in-charge who had a discussion with employees. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a food employee eating in the kitchen area. Although employee stepped back from the counter, eating must occur in designated areas. Inspector observed that designated personal areas are at the desk at the rear of the kitchen where all personal drinks and other personal items are kept. Ensure that eating and drinking only occur in designated areas away from food and food-service areas. Manager corrected behavior on site.

2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Sanitizing temperature
findings.comment:
Observed dishwasher to be unable to reach 180F. PIC stated company told facility the dishwasher was a chemical sanitizing dishwasher. After investigation and testing, no sanitizer is attached to machine. Heat sanitizing dishwashers must reach a minimum of 180F. 
750-830 All hot water for sanitizing dishes and equipment must be a minimum of 180F when it leaves the dishwashing machine manifold in order to kill pathogens.  Properly sanitize all items. Check and maintain the dishwasher frequently.
